frozen_candidate_root_contribution: The state of being denuded / without a covering — bareness: the absence of a concealing or sheltering layer that would normally overlie a surface (a body, a stretch of ground).

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: The state of being denuded / without a covering — bareness: the absence of a concealing or sheltering layer that would normally overlie a surface (a body, a stretch of ground).
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Three occurrences, two lexemes. (1) 20:118 تَعْرَىٰ (form I verb, of Adam in the garden): "you will neither go hungry therein nor be uncovered" — the residue is bodily bareness, lacking clothing that covers. (2) 37:145 and (3) 68:49 بِٱلْعَرَآءِ (verbal noun, of Jonah cast ashore): "We cast him onto al-'arā'" — the open, bare tract of ground, land denuded of vegetation and shelter. Across both lexemes the invariant left after subtracting form and context is one thing: a surface stripped of / lacking the covering that would normally overlie it. For the body that covering is clothing (nakedness); for the land it is vegetation/shelter (barren openness). The concept is identical, only the substrate differs.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: Subtracted layers: (a) FORM — تَعْرَىٰ is form-I imperfect encoding the STATE/becoming of the subject ("to be/come to be bare"); العَرَآء is a verbal noun naming the bare THING/place. Neither the eventive-state nor the nominalized-locus is root content; both host the same "bareness" residue. (b) CONSTRUCTION — بِٱلْعَرَآءِ: the preposition bi- supplies a locative "at/on the bare place"; the negation لَا in 20:118 supplies "not-bare." These framing vectors are not root content. (c) PARTICIPANTS — Adam's body vs. Jonah's landing-ground; the differing substrate (body vs. terrain) is participant/collocation, not root. (d) CONTEXT — Edenic promise vs. eschatological/narrative deliverance-and-rebuke; irrelevant to the residue. Residue after subtraction = "denuded of covering / bare."
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: The two العَرَآء occurrences (37:145, 68:49) apply the root to LAND, not a body, which could look like a different sense ("open shore/plain") than nakedness. It reconciles cleanly: al-'arā' is precisely the ground "naked" of vegetation and shelter — bareness of terrain — the same denuded-of-covering residue applied to a different surface. No form- or context-forcing is needed; both readings are surface-recoverable as bareness.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: Strongest alternative: the core is "exposure to view / openness" (being laid open to sight) rather than "lack of covering." It covers all three (a naked person is exposed; al-'arā' is open ground). Internal arbitration favors bareness: al-'arā' foregrounds absence of shelter/vegetation (Jonah is sick/blameworthy on barren ground), not being-seen; and 20:118 pairs تَعْرَى with تَجُوع (hunger) — both are privations of a basic bodily provision (food, covering), pointing to "lack of covering" over "visibility." Exposure-to-view is a downstream consequence of bareness, not the invariant itself.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Distinct from ك ش ف (k-sh-f, to uncover/remove a cover) and ب د و / ظ ه ر (b-d-w, Z-h-r, to appear/become manifest): those name the ACT of removing a covering or the RESULT of becoming visible, whereas ع ر ي names the resulting STATE of being bare/without covering, agnostic to whether anyone removed it or sees it. It is also distinct from ف ض ح (f-D-H, disgraceful exposure), which adds shame; ع ر ي is neutral physical/spatial bareness. Falsifiability: if a confirmed ع ر ي occurrence denoted the act of stripping a cover off something (leaving the agent/action foregrounded) or denoted becoming-visible without any implication of a surface left bare, the "state-of-bareness" invariant would fail.
internal_discovery.rationale: A single non-empty residue — "denuded of / lacking a covering; bareness" — is surface-recoverable in every one of the 3 occurrences without forcing. The verb تَعْرَى is bodily bareness (nakedness); al-'arā' (twice) is terrain bareness (open, shelterless ground). The extension from body to land is not a stretched metaphor but the identical concept over different substrates, internally bridged by the shared privation notion (in 20:118 bareness is paired with hunger as basic privations). Direction is determinate (absence of covering, not its addition), and the root is sharply distinct from its uncover-act (k-sh-f) and become-visible (b-d-w/Z-h-r) neighbors. No occurrence resists reconciliation; presence is clean and universal across all 3, warranting STRONG.

adversarial_verification.notes: Refutation attempt failed to break the candidate; all 3 occurrences fit tightly. (1) 20:118 تَعْرَىٰ, paired with تَجُوعَ, is bodily bareness = absence of covering clothing — direct fit. (2) 37:145 and (3) 68:49 بِٱلْعَرَآءِ (identical lexeme/context, Jonah cast ashore) denote the open bare tract, ground stripped of vegetation/shelter — the concealing/sheltering layer that would normally overlie it is absent. Hardest case: the verb(body)/noun(land) two-lexeme split, which could look like homonymy. But al-'arā' lexically means the tract LACKING trees/buildings/screening, so the invariant 'surface without its normal overlying cover' is identical across both lexemes — only the substrate (clothing vs. vegetation/shelter) differs. No ad-hoc/circular rescue required. Distinctiveness holds: the contribution discriminates against neighbor senses that DO NOT appear here — عور (visual defect/exposed flaw), عرو/عارية (to befall / a borrowed loan-item). Falsifiable: any occurrence meaning 'loan,' 'befall,' or 'defect' would break it; none present. Two lexemes, one concept, no genuine semantic split.

occurrence_dispositions.note: تَعْرَىٰ paired with تَجُوعَ ('go hungry'): 'you will not be uncovered' = bodily bareness, lacking the clothing that would normally cover the body. Candidate residue (surface stripped of its covering) directly present.
بِٱلْعَرَآءِ in فَنَبَذْنَٰهُ بِٱلْعَرَآءِ — Jonah cast onto the open bare tract, land denuded of vegetation/shelter. Same denuded-surface residue, substrate = ground rather than body.
بِٱلْعَرَآءِ in لَنُبِذَ بِٱلْعَرَآءِ — parallel to 37:145; the bare, sheltering-less open ground. Candidate residue recoverable.
